headline: Chips and Energy Set a Firm Tone as Middle East Risks Hang Over the Open
body_html:
Wall Street returns Tuesday to a market that finished Monday on firm footing, with 337 of the 544 stocks we track higher and 202 lower. Semiconductors led the way, up 2.2%, followed by energy at 1.18% and industrials at 0.64%. Homebuilders were the only sector in the red, down 0.94%.

Overnight attention is on the Middle East. A Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted Houthi missiles and drones aimed at the kingdom, yet oil edged only slightly higher as hopes for diplomacy offset the attacks. Israel's election, and Netanyahu's suggestion that a renewed war on Iran is possible, add another layer of uncertainty for energy traders at the open.

At the open, watch whether Monday's leaders hold their gains. Range Resources jumped 17.66%, while Vicor gained 10.64%, Comfort Systems 7.18%, Everpure 6.49%, Arm 6.19% and Coherent 5.83%. On the other side, Fair Isaac fell 13.15%, Amkor 6.34% and DoorDash 6.1%. Whether chip strength spreads or fades will set the tone.

briefs.headline: Chip Sector Leads, but Not Every Name Follows
briefs.body: Semiconductors topped all sectors Monday with a 2.2% gain, and Arm rose 6.19%. Yet chip packager Amkor slid 6.34%, a reminder that the rally was selective. Traders will look at the open to see whether the strength broadens.

briefs.headline: Natural Gas Producer Posts Standout Surge
briefs.body: Range Resources climbed 17.66% on Monday, the biggest gain in our universe, helping energy stocks advance 1.18% as a group. The question for the open is whether buyers keep pushing or take profits after such a sharp move.

briefs.headline: Fair Isaac Tumbles Over 13%
briefs.body: Fair Isaac dropped 13.15%, the steepest decline among the stocks we track on Monday. The scale of the move makes it a name to watch for any rebound or further selling when trading begins Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Gulf Attacks Meet Diplomatic Hopes in Oil
briefs.body: A Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting Houthi missiles and drones targeting the kingdom. Even so, crude rose only modestly, as hopes for a diplomatic path restrained the move. Energy investors will watch whether that balance survives the morning.

briefs.headline: Israel's Vote Adds Geopolitical Uncertainty
briefs.body: Israelis are voting in an election that could decide Netanyahu's political future. His hint that a war on Iran could restart gives markets a possible escalation risk to price, particularly in energy and defense-sensitive corners.

briefs.headline: Fuel Costs Weigh on Airlines and Politics
briefs.body: JetBlue reported a wider loss because of higher fuel costs, though its chief executive says margins are improving. Separately, a study finds US consumers bear heavy costs from fuel price spikes tied to the Iran war, a theme gaining political weight ahead of the midterms.
